rationale: Needs both Talarico (TX) and El-Sayed (MI) to win. Talarico leads by 2-4 in October polls (Marist, Emerson, UH, TPOR) but Texas has a Republican lean and polls are narrowing (~55%); El-Sayed leads by 2-3 in averages (~65%). Outcomes are positively correlated via national environment, so joint ~0.42. v3: normal case, kept within 0.10-0.90. A search summary quoted market odds for Michigan; discarded.

Minnesota has not elected a Republican senator since 2002 and the national environment favors Democrats. Flanagan leads Tafoya by 3-5 in averages (RCP +3.4, others +4.6 to +5.2), though Cook moved it to Lean D. Polling misses of 4+ points are plausible, so ~0.80. v3: normal case, within 0.10-0.90.

Meeting is Oct 28-29, three days out. Analyst previews (FXStreet, Reuters economist poll) expect a hold at 2.50% with the next hike seen in December; the ECB rarely surprises against clear guidance this close to a meeting. v3: nearly-settled case (too little time left), so allowed at 0.05. Search results showed futures-implied pricing; discarded.

Status quo is the fragile ceasefire holding; Netanyahu said no preemptive strike before Israel's Oct 27 election and Trump reportedly opposes restarting the war before the Nov 3 midterms. But both US and Israel are openly threatening renewed strikes, talks have stalled, Hormuz attacks peaked in October, and the window extends 12 days past the midterms. ~0.62. v3: normal case.

South Carolina is strongly Republican (base rate for R Senate wins near-certain), but this special after Lindsey Graham's death features appointee Darline Graham vs Annie Andrews, who has outraised her ~7-to-1. Polls show Graham +1 to +3 on average with a D-internal showing Andrews +1; Republicans usually outperform polls slightly in SC. ~0.68. v3: normal case.

Ohio has trended Republican (base rate favors R), but Acton leads Ramaswamy in most October polls (Marist +7, BGSU +6, VoteHub +4; RCP avg +4.4) with one ActiVote outlier at R+2.8; Sabato moved to Lean D. Ohio polls historically underestimate Republicans by a few points, so ~0.66. v3: normal case. A search summary quoted market odds; discarded.

Republicans hold 53-47 and need only 50 with the VP. Non-market models give Democrats 56-76% (Poliwave 57, DDHQ 56, VoteHub 60, Silver ~76) with Pollsmax the outlier at R 54.5%; Democrats lead narrowly in many must-win races (TX, OH, AK, NC etc.) where a polling miss could flip several together. ~0.38 for R. v3: normal case. A search summary quoted market odds; discarded.

Five days remain. Only a local humanitarian truce in Oleshky (excluded as not a general pause) has been agreed; the next trilateral round is planned for mid-November in Abu Dhabi and the Kremlin says no restrictions on combat operations until a comprehensive deal. v3: nearly-settled case (too little time left), so below 0.05.

Incumbent senators usually win (base rate ~85-90%), but Peltola entered and averages show a near-tie with Peltola +0.8 to +2.4 (RCP, Pollsmax, Poliwave), with individual polls split and Trump campaigning for Sullivan. Alaska polls have historically underestimated Republicans, and RCV adds uncertainty. ~0.45. v3: normal case. A search result quoted market odds; discarded.

As of Oct 25 no official anthropic.com/news announcement; latest Fable is 5.1. Asks the probability that no US-Iran Hormuz agreement is announced by Nov 2. Talks have stalled for weeks, Iran says the strait stays closed until its seven conditions are met, and the US has added demands; Trump wants no escalation before midterms but a full mutual agreement in 7 days is unlikely. v3: nearly-settled case (one week left, stalled talks), so slightly above 0.90.

Fighting escalated in October (Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport, barrage Oct 25). There is an unconfirmed report of a Saudi $1B Iran-brokered offer to halt attacks, but Riyadh officially rejects a new ceasefire, and both sides must announce acceptance within five days. v3: nearly-settled case (too little time left), set at 0.08 rather than lower because active back-channel talks are reported.
